# Susan Baker

## Overview

- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v2 c1 P0](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0000)</sub>
- **Status:** Unmarried  <sub>[v2 c11 P3](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0003), [v2 c22 P4](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0004)</sub>
- **Role:** Housekeeper and maid-of-all-work at Ingleside  <sub>[v2 c1 P0](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0000), [v4 c18 P28](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0028)</sub>

## Appearance

Susan Baker is a tall, gray, and grim woman with a sharp face and an unhomely appearance. She wears an apron while performing her household duties.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P0](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0000), [v2 c11 P3](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0003), [v4 c15 P0](../source/v04-c15.md#nw-v04-c15-p0000), [v4 c30 P22](../source/v04-c30.md#nw-v04-c30-p0022)_

## Personality

Susan is a deeply faithful, hard-working, and fiercely devoted woman who takes intense pride in her housekeeping and culinary skills. Though often grim, pessimistic, and stubborn, she harbors a deeply affectionate and protective nature towards those in her care, particularly the children. She is intensely loyal to the Blythe family and holds firm, traditional Presbyterian views.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P0](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0000), [v2 c1 P6](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0006), [v2 c7 P21](../source/v02-c07.md#nw-v02-c07-p0021), [v4 c18 P28](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0028), [v4 c40 P6](../source/v04-c40.md#nw-v04-c40-p0006), [v5 c1 P5](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0005)_

## Goals

- To faithfully serve and manage the household of Dr. Gilbert and Anne Blythe  <sub>[v4 c19 P10](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0010), [v5 c1 P8](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0008)</sub>

## History

Susan Baker was engaged as the maid-of-all-work and housekeeper for Dr. Gilbert Blythe and Anne Shirley at their first home in Four Winds. She took complete charge of the domestic management of the household, priding herself on her culinary accomplishments and dedicated service. When Anne gave birth to her son Shirley after a life-threatening illness, Susan nursed the infant constantly and claimed him as her special nursling. She later moved with the family to their new home at Ingleside in Glen St. Mary. During the Blythes' three-month trip to Europe, Susan cared for Shirley at her brother's home while the other children visited Avonlea. Upon their return, she resumed her position as the indispensable pillar of the Ingleside household.

_Sources: [v4 c18 P28](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0028), [v4 c22 P1](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0001), [v4 c40 P42](../source/v04-c40.md#nw-v04-c40-p0042), [v5 c1 P0](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0000), [v5 c1 P5](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0005), [v5 c1 P6](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0006), [v5 c1 P8](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0008)_

## Quotes

> You tell young Mrs. Doctor not to worry about a single thing—Susan is at the helm. You tell her just to think of her baby.  <sub>[v4 c19 P10](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0010)</sub>

> I have had as much experience with him as you, Mrs. Doctor, dear, have I not?  <sub>[v4 c35 P19](../source/v04-c35.md#nw-v04-c35-p0019)</sub>

> I gave him life just as much as you did, Mrs. Dr. dear. He is just as much my baby as he is yours.  <sub>[v5 c1 P5](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0005)</sub>

> I have never found that Methodism was catching.  <sub>[v5 c15 P22](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0022)</sub>
